title: JSON suppression mishandles the opening brace and drops or suppresses following text
reasoning: The processor sets _json_brace_depth to 1 when it sees an opening brace, but in the mid-chunk path it recursively processes post_marker including that same opening brace. The JSON suppression branch increments depth again, so a normal one-object JSON payload never returns to zero on its closing brace and all following text in that chunk is dropped. In the initial buffering path, a complete buffered JSON object with trailing natural language is dropped wholesale without scanning for the matching closing brace, so speech after JSON can be lost.
reproduction: After the processor is in text mode, process a chunk like 'Intro {"x":1} outro'. 'Intro ' is sent, but the opening brace is counted twice and ' outro' is not sent. Starting from the indeterminate state with '{"x":1} outro' drops the entire buffer and does not recover ' outro'.
recommendation: Use one consistent JSON parser state transition: either consume the opening brace before entering suppression with depth 1, or enter with depth 0 and let the suppression scanner count the included content. Also scan the current buffered content for JSON completion so trailing non-JSON text can be passed through.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are present, and the edge cases with JSON beginning mid-chunk or completing in the initial buffer are not evidenced by any included test.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests asserting that 'Intro {"x":1} outro' and '{"x":1} outro' suppress only the JSON object and still send the surrounding text to TTS.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/processing/tts/processor.py JSON brace-depth handling plus focused TTSProcessor tests.
